doc: Slack-style conversation components: a message, a thread, and a channel's history.

capabilities.reason: profile pictures from the three origins Slack serves them on — ca.slack-edge.com, avatars.slack-edge.com and secure.gravatar.com. All three are literals in Message's view; a profile only ever supplies the path, and a picture anywhere else is not drawn.

components.name: Segment
components.doc: One styled run of a message body: plain, bold, italic, struck, code, a mention, a channel reference or a link.

messageDocs.name: open
messageDocs.doc: Report this segment's URL upwards; a link segment cannot navigate by itself.

messageDocs.name: segClass
messageDocs.doc: The utility classes this run's flags add up to.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The literal text of the run.

fields.name: bold
fields.doc: Render bold.

fields.name: italic
fields.doc: Render italic.

fields.name: strike
fields.doc: Render struck through.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: Render as inline code.

fields.name: mention
fields.doc: This run names a person.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: This run names a channel.

fields.name: link
fields.doc: This run is a link; clicking it emits openLink.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: Where the link points. Reported, never followed.

inits.name: link
inits.doc: A link — clicking it emits openLink rather than navigating.

components.name: Scope
components.doc: What an answer covers and what it never looked at: which conversation kinds were read, how many, and whether a cap stopped it. Not an error and not a warning — the sentence that turns a count into a claim someone can check.

messageDocs.name: hasAny
messageDocs.doc: Whether there is anything to disclose at all.

messageDocs.name: kindsLabel
messageDocs.doc: Which conversation kinds were searched.

messageDocs.name: hasScanned
messageDocs.doc: Whether anybody counted the conversations that were read.

messageDocs.name: scannedLabel
messageDocs.doc: How many were read.

messageDocs.name: hasDmNote
messageDocs.doc: Whether to say that DMs were never in the set. The absence is the disclosure.

messageDocs.name: dmLabel
messageDocs.doc: That DMs and group DMs are never included.

messageDocs.name: truncatedLabel
messageDocs.doc: What stopped the scan early, spelled out.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: Everything this scope discloses, as one line — the card's tooltip.

fields.name: publicChannels
fields.doc: Public channels were in the set.

fields.name: privateChannels
fields.doc: The private channels this token was invited to were in the set.

fields.name: dms
fields.doc: DMs and group DMs were in the set. False by default, and that is a statement about the tools rather than about the token: `conversations.list` is asked for public and private channels, so an `im` is never in the set whatever the token could have seen.

fields.name: channelsScanned
fields.doc: How many conversations were actually read. Absent means nobody counted, which is not the same as zero.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: A cap stopped the scan before the data ran out. The field that matters most: the difference between "there is no more" and "I stopped looking".

fields.name: truncatedBy
fields.doc: What stopped it, in the caller's own words — `limit`, `max_search_channels`.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: Anything else worth saying, in one sentence.

inits.name: a search that stopped early
inits.doc: Eleven conversations out of a workspace nobody counted, DMs never in the set, and a cap that stopped the scan — the three facts a results card used to leave entirely to the prose.

inits.name: one channel, read whole
inits.doc: The quiet case: nothing was truncated, and the only thing worth saying is the one thing that is always true.

components.name: RichText
components.doc: A message body: a flat list of styled segments, rendered as one run of text.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: The runs that make up this body, in order.

inits.name: mixed
inits.doc: Every segment style in one body.

components.name: Reaction
components.doc: One emoji reaction with its count. Clicking it toggles your own and tells whoever is above.

messageDocs.name: toggle
messageDocs.doc: Add or take back your reaction, and report it upwards.

fields.name: emoji
fields.doc: The emoji.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many people reacted.

fields.name: reacted
fields.doc: Whether you are one of them.

inits.name: mine
inits.doc: One you are already part of.

components.name: Message
components.doc: A single message: who wrote it, when, its rich-text body and its reactions. Compact styling is what a threaded reply uses.

messageDocs.name: initials
messageDocs.doc: Up to two initials for the avatar disc. The picture is drawn OVER it, so this is what a message with no picture — or one a fetch fails on — shows.

messageDocs.name: slackCdnPath
messageDocs.doc: The avatar's path on ca.slack-edge.com, or empty. One of these three is non-empty at most, and the view pairs each with the origin it named.

messageDocs.name: slackAvatarsPath
messageDocs.doc: The same for avatars.slack-edge.com.

messageDocs.name: gravatarPath
messageDocs.doc: The same for secure.gravatar.com, which is where Slack's default pictures live.

messageDocs.name: authorLabel
messageDocs.doc: The author as @name.

messageDocs.name: channelLabel
messageDocs.doc: The channel as #name.

messageDocs.name: hasChannel
messageDocs.doc: Whether to show the channel badge — a reply never does.

messageDocs.name: timeLabel
messageDocs.doc: The clock time, sliced out of createdAt.

messageDocs.name: openPermalink
messageDocs.doc: Ask for this message's permalink to be opened; emits `openLink` with the url. This bundle cannot navigate to a workspace it cannot name.

messageDocs.name: hasId
messageDocs.doc: Whether there is a timestamp to show. The `ts` is the argument every follow-up call takes, so the card draws it rather than only carrying it.

messageDocs.name: idTitle
messageDocs.doc: What the timestamp is for, spelled out.

messageDocs.name: hasPermalink
messageDocs.doc: Whether there is a link to offer.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable id of the message.

fields.name: author
fields.doc: Who wrote it.

fields.name: avatar
fields.doc: The author's picture, as the full url a Slack profile carries. Drawn when it is on one of the three origins the view names; the initials show through when it is not, and when there is none.

fields.name: channelName
fields.doc: The channel it was posted in.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: ISO 8601 timestamp, as it arrived. No clock is read.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The rich-text body. Accepts a RichText object or a bare segment list.

fields.name: reactions
fields.doc: The reactions on this message.

fields.name: compact
fields.doc: Reply styling: tighter, and no channel badge.

fields.name: edited
fields.doc: Show the (edited) marker.

fields.name: pinned
fields.doc: Show the pinned badge.

fields.name: permalink
fields.doc: The workspace archive link for this message. Shown and clickable, and still not an `href`: a permalink is `https://<team>.slack.com/archives/...` and the subdomain is the workspace's, so there is no origin a view can write as a literal. Clicking it emits `openLink`, exactly as a link segment does.

inits.doc: The same message as a threaded reply: compact, no channel badge.

inits.name: empty
inits.doc: Nobody, nothing — what an unfilled placeholder looks like.

inits.name: with a timestamp and a link
inits.doc: The two things a message always carried and never drew: the `ts` every follow-up call takes, and the archive link — which is offered and still not followed, because a workspace subdomain is not an origin a view can name.

components.name: Thread
components.doc: A root message and its replies, with the replies foldable.

messageDocs.name: toggle
messageDocs.doc: Fold or unfold the replies.

messageDocs.name: setExpanded
messageDocs.doc: Fold or unfold from outside — what a channel's expand-all sends.

messageDocs.name: hasReplies
messageDocs.doc: Whether there are any replies.

messageDocs.name: replyLabel
messageDocs.doc: The fold button's caret and count.

messageDocs.name: openThread
messageDocs.doc: Ask for the replies that were counted but not fetched; emits `openThread` with the channel and the timestamp that would fetch them.

messageDocs.name: hasUnloadedReplies
messageDocs.doc: There is a reply count and no replies behind it — the state a collapsed one-message thread is always in.

messageDocs.name: loadLabel
messageDocs.doc: That the replies were counted and not loaded.

messageDocs.name: loadTitle
messageDocs.doc: The two arguments that would load them, filled in.

fields.name: root
fields.doc: The message the thread hangs off.

fields.name: replies
fields.doc: The replies, oldest first. Each is forced compact.

fields.name: expanded
fields.doc: Whether the replies are showing.

fields.name: replyCount
fields.doc: How many replies EXIST, which is not how many arrived. `conversations.history` answers with roots carrying a count and never with the replies themselves, so a card built from one has a number and nothing behind it. Absent, it is taken from the replies that did arrive — which for a thread read whole is the same number.

fields.name: channelName
fields.doc: Which conversation the root is in, so a thread whose replies were not fetched can say the argument that would fetch them. Defaults to the root message's own `channelName`.

fields.name: rootTs
fields.doc: The root's timestamp, for the same reason. Defaults to the root message's own `id`.

inits.doc: Exactly what `conversations.history` hands a card: a root with twenty-one replies counted and none of them fetched. The caret is not offered — there is nothing behind it — and what is offered instead is the call that would fetch them.

components.name: FileList
components.doc: The files a channel or a search turned up: what each one is, who uploaded it, and where it lives. Metadata only — nothing in this bundle can hand anybody a file's contents, and the card says so rather than looking as though it could.

messageDocs.name: openFile
messageDocs.doc: Ask for one row's permalink to be opened, by its position in the list; emits `openLink`.

messageDocs.name: title
messageDocs.doc: What is being listed.

messageDocs.name: countLabel
messageDocs.doc: How many files there are.

messageDocs.name: isEmpty
messageDocs.doc: Whether there are none.

messageDocs.name: note
messageDocs.doc: That the bytes are not available through this server.

fields.name: filter
fields.doc: What was being listed — a channel name, a person — for the header. Empty for whatever the token can see.

fields.name: files
fields.doc: The files, each `{ id, name, title, mimetype, size, author, createdAt, permalink }`. A row's label is the title if there is one, the filename if there is not, and the id if there is neither.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this listing covers. Same record shape a ChannelHistory's scope takes.

inits.name: a channel’s files

components.name: ChannelHistory
components.doc: One channel's conversations: a header, a filter box, an ordering toggle and the threads themselves.

messageDocs.name: setQuery
messageDocs.doc: Narrow the stream to threads whose text contains this.

messageDocs.name: toggleOrder
messageDocs.doc: Flip between newest-first and oldest-first.

messageDocs.name: expandAll
messageDocs.doc: Unfold every thread currently shown.

messageDocs.name: collapseAll
messageDocs.doc: Fold every thread currently shown.

messageDocs.name: openLink
messageDocs.doc: A segment somewhere below asked for a URL to be opened.

messageDocs.name: reacted
messageDocs.doc: A reaction somewhere below was toggled.

messageDocs.name: channelLabel
messageDocs.doc: The channel as #name.

messageDocs.name: memberLabel
messageDocs.doc: The member count as a sentence.

messageDocs.name: orderLabel
messageDocs.doc: The ordering toggle's label.

messageDocs.name: countLabel
messageDocs.doc: How many threads are shown, of how many.

messageDocs.name: hasError
messageDocs.doc: Whether the error banner shows.

messageDocs.name: isEmpty
messageDocs.doc: Whether the empty-state line shows.

messageDocs.name: openThread
messageDocs.doc: A thread asked for replies it was counted but not given. The channel history is the one that can say which call would fetch them, so it stops the bubble and says so in its footer.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: The channel name, without the #.

fields.name: topic
fields.doc: The channel topic.

fields.name: memberCount
fields.doc: How many people are in it.

fields.name: threads
fields.doc: The conversations currently shown — filtered and ordered.

fields.name: query
fields.doc: The filter text. Empty shows everything.

fields.name: newestFirst
fields.doc: Order by root timestamp, newest first.

fields.name: loading
fields.doc: Show the loading banner.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Show this as an error banner. Empty shows none.

fields.name: lastAction
fields.doc: The last thing a child reported, shown in the footer.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this answer covers and what it never looked at. Written as a plain record whose keys are the Scope component's own field names; drawn only when there is something to disclose.
